scope: Batch B MEDIUM 2, round 2: 1694091d, src/render/attackFx/styles/yoriko.js onImpact (Yoriko's marionette Strike cut). 844x390 only.
summary: The cut still reads as a long WHITE blade with a lilac fringe, the same look as round 1. The cause is a mix-up over what asp does. In QuadPool, asp multiplies the WIDTH (w = s * asp; the height stays s). So 'b.asp = 7' does not make the edge narrow. It makes the additive white edge about 7x as long as it is tall: about 2.4-2.8 tiles long and 0.34-0.4 tiles tall. The core is about 0.9 x 0.46 tiles. At alpha 0.35 in additive blend, the long blade turns the light road and the enemy's white body flash to near white. It also lies over the lilac core and sums it to white. A diagnostic run (core tinted red, edge alpha 0, local only and reverted) has no white blade at all. That proves the blade is the edge sprite. The deeper lilac core itself works: where it is not covered it reads lilac and stays visible over the white body (3x next frame).

findings.where: src/render/attackFx/styles/yoriko.js onImpact, the EDGE sprite (b): spr(bbA, ..., s * 0.85, s, 0.08, EDGE, 0.35) with b.asp = 7
findings.what: asp is the width/height ratio (QuadPool.update: w = s * asp, height = s). asp 7 at size 0.85s-1s gives an additive white blade about 6-7x the core's length (core: asp 2.2 at s-1.15s). It sweeps across the road and the enemy and turns the cut white. MEDIUM 2 is still open.
findings.fix: To make the edge thin, shrink its size (the height) and keep its length near the core's. For example, s0 = s * 0.35, s1 = s * 0.4, asp ~5.5-6, so the width is about 2.2s, the same as the core. Or move it to the crescent's outer rim, or drop it. Then re-check at 844x390 that the cut reads lilac on the hit frame.
